name: Arduino Pro Mini clone (ATmega328P)
description: Ultra-cheap $2-3 ATmega328P Uno-class board in a 33 x 18 mm package with 20 I/O and 8 ADC channels; no USB, so budget a $1-2 serial adapter, but ideal for permanent low-power projects.
notes: No USB: program through the 6-pin header with an FTDI/CH340/CP2102 adapter (DTR auto-reset). The adapter is not included.
Two versions: 5 V / 16 MHz and 3.3 V / 8 MHz; I/O voltage follows the version (table lists the 5 V one). Check the regulator/resonator markings.
14 digital pins and 6 analog pins (A0-A5) are usable as GPIO; A6/A7 are analog-input only (extra ADC channels). I2C is A4/A5 on inner pads.
Clone quality varies (ceramic resonator, counterfeit 328 chips); no header data due to the 4-group (sides, FTDI, inner pad) layout.
